subject: Economy
sub_topic: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs — CBIC

concepts.name: Statutory Origin and Organizational Structure of CBIC
key_dimensions: Established under Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 — distinction from CBDT which shares the same parent act
Renamed from CBEC to CBIC in 2018 via Finance Act to reflect expanded GST mandate
Position as a statutory body under Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance — not a constitutional body
UPSC trap: CBIC vs CBDT — both under Ministry of Finance but CBIC handles indirect taxes, CBDT handles direct taxes

concepts.name: Jurisdictional Mandate: Indirect Taxes Administered by CBIC
key_dimensions: Post-GST mandate: Central GST (CGST), Integrated GST (IGST), Customs duty, and Central Excise on excluded products (petroleum, liquor)
Pre-GST mandate included Central Excise, Service Tax, and Customs — understanding the shift is critical
UPSC trap: GST on petroleum products is NOT yet levied — CBIC still administers Central Excise on these
Distinction between taxes subsumed into GST vs taxes still outside GST framework

concepts.name: CBIC's Role in GST Administration: Division of Taxpayer Base
key_dimensions: 90:10 formula — States administer 90% of taxpayers below ₹1.5 crore turnover threshold; Centre administers 10%
Above ₹1.5 crore threshold — 50:50 split between Centre (CBIC) and States
IGST exclusively administered by CBIC since it is a Central subject
UPSC trap: This division is for CGST/SGST administration, not for IGST — IGST is entirely Central

concepts.name: Customs Act, 1962 and CBIC's Enforcement Powers
key_dimensions: CBIC administers Customs Act, 1962 — powers of search, seizure, arrest, and adjudication
Customs duty rates set by Customs Tariff Act, 1975 — CBIC administers but does NOT set rates (Finance Ministry/Parliament does)
CBIC issues Customs notifications, circulars, and tariff classifications under HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature)
UPSC trap: CBIC administers customs but the rates are determined by the Union Budget — policy vs administration distinction

concepts.name: GST Network (GSTN) and CBIC: Functional Relationship
key_dimensions: GSTN is the IT backbone for GST — a non-profit, non-government company (recently converted to 100% government ownership)
CBIC uses GSTN for registration, return filing, and compliance monitoring but does NOT own or control GSTN
CBIC's ACES (Automation of Central Excise and Service Tax) portal preceded GSTN — now largely replaced
UPSC trap: GSTN is NOT under CBIC — it is a separate entity; CBIC is a policy/enforcement body, GSTN is the technology platform

concepts.name: Project Saksham: CBIC's IT Modernization Initiative
key_dimensions: CBIC's umbrella IT modernization project — includes GSTN integration, new Customs IT system (ICEGATE upgrade), and ACES-GST
Aimed at creating a single interface for taxpayers across GST and Customs
Implemented with World Bank assistance — international funding angle relevant for GS2/GS3
UPSC relevance: Example of technology-driven tax administration reform — often cited in governance and economy questions

concepts.name: ICEGATE: Indian Customs EDI Gateway
key_dimensions: Electronic Data Interchange portal for Customs — enables e-filing of import/export documents, bill of entry, shipping bills
Facilitates Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) compliance — reduces dwell time at ports
Integrated with other agencies: DGFT, Port Trusts, Banks — single window concept
UPSC trap: ICEGATE is for Customs only — it is NOT the GST portal; confusing ICEGATE with GSTN is a common error

concepts.name: Faceless Assessment Scheme under Customs (2020)
key_dimensions: Introduced in 2020 — Customs assessment decoupled from port of import; done by officers at any location
Reduces physical interface between importer and officer — anti-corruption measure
Modelled on Income Tax faceless assessment but applied to Customs — comparison angle for UPSC
UPSC relevance: Ease of Doing Business, Trade Facilitation, and reducing inspector raj — connects to multiple GS3 themes

concepts.name: Anti-Smuggling and Enforcement Directorate General: DRI
key_dimensions: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) functions under CBIC — premier anti-smuggling intelligence agency
DRI vs ED (Enforcement Directorate) — DRI handles Customs Act violations; ED handles FEMA and PMLA — critical distinction
DRI vs NCB — DRI handles smuggling of all goods including drugs under Customs Act; NCB specifically handles narcotics under NDPS Act
UPSC trap: Multiple enforcement agencies under different ministries — DRI (CBIC/Finance), ED (Finance), NCB (Home Ministry)

concepts.name: GST Council and CBIC: Policy vs. Administration Distinction
key_dimensions: GST Council is a constitutional body (Article 279A) that recommends GST rates and policies — CBIC implements these recommendations
CBIC issues circulars and notifications to operationalize GST Council decisions — subordinate legislation role
CBIC Chairman is a key participant in GST Council meetings but GST Council is NOT part of CBIC
UPSC trap: GST Council decides policy; CBIC administers — conflating the two bodies is a common conceptual error

concepts.name: CBIC's Role in Trade Facilitation and WTO-TFA Compliance
key_dimensions: India ratified WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) in 2016 — CBIC is the primary implementation agency
Key TFA measures implemented by CBIC: Single Window Interface for Facilitating Trade (SWIFT), Risk Management System (RMS), Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) programme
AEO Programme: Trusted trader status for compliant importers/exporters — tiered system (AEO-T1, T2, T3, LO)
UPSC relevance: India's improvement in Logistics Performance Index (LPI) linked to CBIC's trade facilitation measures

concepts.name: Risk Management System (RMS) in Customs
key_dimensions: RMS selects consignments for examination based on risk parameters — reduces 100% physical examination
Enables 'green channel' (no examination), 'yellow channel' (document check), 'red channel' (physical examination)
Balances facilitation for compliant traders with enforcement against smuggling/evasion
UPSC trap: RMS is under CBIC/Customs — it is NOT the same as the Risk-Based Supervision used by financial regulators like RBI or SEBI

concepts.name: Anti-Profiteering Mechanism and CBIC's Role
key_dimensions: Anti-Profiteering Authority (now Competition Commission of India after 2022 merger) ensured GST rate reduction benefits passed to consumers
CBIC's Directorate General of Anti-Profiteering (DGAP) investigated complaints and submitted reports to the authority
UPSC trap: After November 2022, anti-profiteering cases under GST are handled by CCI — not a separate authority; CBIC still investigates via DGAP
Connects to consumer protection and GST reform — relevant for both GS2 (governance) and GS3 (economy)

concepts.name: Customs Duty Structure: Types and Exemptions
key_dimensions: Basic Customs Duty (BCD), Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS — 10% of BCD), IGST on imports, Compensation Cess on imports — layered structure
UPSC trap: CVD (Countervailing Duty) and SAD (Special Additional Duty) were subsumed into IGST post-GST — pre-GST vs post-GST structure
Effective Rate of Duty = BCD + SWS + IGST — understanding cascading vs non-cascading nature
Customs duty exemptions notified under Section 25 of Customs Act — CBIC administers these exemptions

concepts.name: CBIC and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) / Customs Bonded Warehouses
key_dimensions: SEZs are treated as 'deemed foreign territory' for Customs purposes — CBIC administers customs procedures in SEZs
Customs Bonded Warehouses allow deferral of duty payment — CBIC grants licenses and monitors compliance
Private Freight Stations (PFSs) and Inland Container Depots (ICDs) — CBIC's role in regulating these logistics nodes
UPSC trap: SEZ policy is under Ministry of Commerce (DPIIT), but Customs administration within SEZs is under CBIC — policy vs. administration overlap

concepts.name: GST Audit and Investigation: CBIC's Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI)
key_dimensions: DGGI is the GST equivalent of DRI — investigates GST evasion cases across India
DGGI vs State GST enforcement — jurisdiction overlap for cases involving multiple states or large evasion amounts
CBIC issues Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for GST audit — distinction between audit (compliance) and investigation (enforcement)
UPSC trap: DGGI handles GST evasion; DRI handles Customs/smuggling — both under CBIC but different mandates

concepts.name: Advance Ruling Mechanism under Customs and GST
key_dimensions: Advance Ruling Authority allows importers/taxpayers to get binding rulings on duty classification before transactions
Under Customs: Authority for Advance Rulings (AAR) — under CBIC's administrative framework
Under GST: AAR at State level, Appellate AAR at Centre-State joint level — CBIC participates in appellate body
UPSC relevance: Reduces litigation, promotes certainty — connects to Ease of Doing Business rankings

concepts.name: Drawback and Refund Mechanisms: CBIC's Role in Export Promotion
key_dimensions: Duty Drawback Scheme (administered by CBIC) — refunds Customs and Central Excise duties paid on inputs used in exported goods
IGST refund on exports — CBIC processes refunds for exporters who paid IGST on zero-rated supplies
UPSC trap: Duty Drawback (CBIC) vs MEIS/RoDTEP (DGFT/Commerce Ministry) — both are export incentives but administered by different bodies
RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) replaced MEIS — CBIC involved in implementation as it covers indirect tax remission

concepts.name: CBIC's Appellate Hierarchy and Dispute Resolution
key_dimensions: Appeals chain: Adjudicating Authority → Commissioner (Appeals) → Customs/Excise/GST Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) → High Court → Supreme Court
CESTAT: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal — handles pre-GST legacy cases and Customs disputes
UPSC trap: For GST disputes, appellate mechanism differs — GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) is being set up separately from CESTAT
GST Appellate Tribunal delayed setup is a current affairs angle — relevant for 2024-25 UPSC cycle

concepts.name: CBIC Circulars, Notifications, and Subordinate Legislation
key_dimensions: Notifications have the force of law (issued under parent Acts like CGST Act, Customs Act) — Circulars are clarificatory and binding on officers but not on courts
UPSC trap: A Circular cannot override a Notification — courts have held that Circulars cannot contradict the statute or notifications
CBIC issues tariff classification rulings via circulars — important for determining applicable duty rates
Recent CBIC circulars on GST rate rationalization post-GST Council decisions are frequently tested in current affairs
